title: Wire Redis presence service into authenticated WebSocket handler

spec.problem: GET /ws/presence upgrades and the real learner page sends presence:heartbeat, but no Redis presence is recorded because httpserver constructs realtime.Server without attaching Dependencies.PresenceService to PresenceHandler.

acceptance.text: Add an integration regression that fails before the fix when an authenticated session upgrades and heartbeat is sent but Redis remains offline; the failing assertion must identify missing service wiring.
Wire the existing Redis-backed PresenceService to the realtime handler using the smallest compatible API; do not change WebSocket protocol or auth policy.

After fix, authenticated upgrade marks the user online, heartbeat refreshes last-seen, and closing the last connection clears online state; preserve anonymous rejection and multi-connection semantics.

spec.expected_behavior: HTTP server composition passes Dependencies.PresenceService to /ws/presence; connect and heartbeat update Redis, last disconnect marks offline.
spec.observed_behavior: Real headed browser upgraded successfully and sent presence:heartbeat, but disposable learner id was absent from Redis presence:online and presence:last_seen; rg confirms the app constructs PresenceService but no caller invokes PresenceHandler.SetService.
spec.rollback_plan: Revert the HTTP-server wiring and its regression test; no schema or persistent canonical content changes.

red_targets.expect: timed out waiting for connected learner to be online
reconnect wrote online while the prior disconnect was still removing it

risk_acknowledgements.reason: The Redis integration is optional when no isolated test Redis is configured, following the existing TEST_DATABASE_URL integration-test pattern. The canonical local RED/GREEN and full Go verification use TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/15, an isolated database on the confirmed local Redis service; no production Redis data is touched.

The Redis integration is optional when TEST_REDIS_URL is absent, following the existing integration-test convention. Canonical RED/GREEN and full verification run it against isolated local Redis DB 15; no production Redis data is touched.
